name: Redis-first live data layer
description:
Reduce DB UPDATE frequency by moving high-churn live data (TradingSignal metadata, position meta, dashboard stats) to Redis-first with throttled/periodic DB persistence. The development.log shows ~3,500 UPDATEs vs 24 SELECTs in a 50MB sample — 93% are solid_queue heartbeats, but the remaining 67 position_tracker updates and massive TradingSignal metadata JSON overwrites are the real pain points. Position PnL is already Redis-cached (RedisPnlCache with 30s DB sync throttle) and ticks are Redis-cached (RedisTickCache). The gap is:

1. TradingSignal.metadata gets rewritten as a giant JSON blob on every signal evaluation cycle (every tick/signal) — even for skipped signals. Move to Redis hash per signal, only persist to DB on resolution/entry/exit.
2. DashboardController still queries PositionTracker aggregates directly for stats — should read from RedisPnlCache + Positions::ActiveCache.
3. position_trackers.meta JSON still gets updated for things like telegram milestones and exit metadata — should batch in Redis.
4. public_ip_logs.last_seen_at gets updated every ~15m — trivial Redis candidate.

Goal: cut non-SolidQueue DB UPDATEs by 80%+ during live trading hours, reflect live data to UI via existing ActionCable + Redis caches, and only persist to DB when state transitions (entry, exit, signal resolution) occur.
